# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1120
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1120
- **Title**: gh-1114 SM: layered tick order + merge-first capacity — freshness before verdicts, merge path reserved (minimal, no semantic changes)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1114` → `main`
- **State**: closed
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +1601
- **Deletions**: -66
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T19:27:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T23:45:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1114
### What changed
Layered the SM tick (gh-1114): `sm_github.json` rules now run in layers — L0 hygiene → **L1 freshness** (unarm-stale / silent-update / park-reset) → L2 verdict (merge / fail / arm / sweep) → L3 dispatch → L4 agents → L5 close — so a head that this tick's freshness rules moved can never be judged by verdicts that read the superseded head (live #435 false park). Added a merge-first capacity reservation so agent lanes can no longer outrun the approved merge path under the workflow cap.

### Key decisions
- New pure leaf module `js/common/smRuleLayers.js`: rule-id → layer map, verdict-action set, merge-path predicate, `mergeReservedSlots`/`reservationFor` math (hoisted require, gh-823 rule)
- `movedThisTick` guard (AC7/AC12): only verified moves record (fresh post-push `github_get_pr` read — E1/E4); DRY ticks never record or claim deferrals (E3); fresh (non-approved) validations keep today's same-tick flow
- L1→L2 boundary drops the `openPrs` ioCache so verdict queries re-read current heads
- Merge-first capacity (AC9-13): reservation held upfront from the dispatch budget; released unused at the L3 boundary (I7) or fully after a merge; in gh-837 parallel mode it equals `validationMutexMax`; `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots: 0` restores today's behavior bit-for-bit (jira-mode ticks never reserve)
- Rule order moved exactly one rule class (unarm-stale-validation into L1, ahead of merge-validated — disjoint query sets, no merge lost); #682/#637/red-yields-slot/gh-994 relative orders preserved and pinned by tests

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smTickLayers.json   # UT-1/AC6 layer-map suite (new)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # full suite: 4764 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  R["sm_github.json rules"] --> L["smRuleLayers.js layer map"]
  L --> T["SM tick (action)"]
  T --> L1["L1 freshness: unarm / silent-update / park-reset"]
  L1 -->|"head moved → tickMovedPrs + openPrs cache drop"| L2["L2 verdict: merge / fail / arm / sweep"]
  L2 -->|"movedThisTick → defer (AC7)"| L3["L3 dispatch: validate-armed before fresh (AC13)"]
  L3 -->|"reservation released / spent"| L4["L4 agent legs (capacity-aware)"]
  L4 --> L5["L5 close"]
```
</details>

+ *                 rework-on-validation-failed, sweep-stale-validating

+ *                 validated-green

+ *   L5 close      close-on-merge

+ * (jobParams.mergeReservedSlots, or the whole gh-837 parallel width) is
+ * reserved for the approved merge path. L4 dispatch rules and fresh

+ * same tick (no idle cap).

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1120._

> ℹ️ **6 resolved thread(s) excluded; 11 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the `mergeReservedSlots: 0` kill switch is inert in gh-837 parallel mode**

`mergeReservedSlots` documents `0` / `false` / `'false'` as *disabling* the reservation — "bit-identical with the pre-gh-1114 capacity behavior" (this module's own docstring at line 156, the PR description, and the ticket's rollback story all rely on it). But `reservationFor` ignores the disabled value whenever parallel validation is active:

```js
function reservationFor(mergeSlots, validationMutexMax) {
    var slots = mergeSlots || 0;
    var mutexMax = validationMutexMax || 1;
    return mutexMax > 1 ? mutexMax : slots;   // slots=0 is overridden when mutexMax>1
}
```

So a project that sets `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots: 0` (or `false`) as an emergency kill switch **still reserves the whole parallel width** on every gh-837 tick: agent lanes are throttled to `initial − validationMutexMax` until the L3 boundary, and when a merge-path validation dispatches, one unit of the cap is held for the whole tick. That is not "today's behavior bit-for-bit".

Note the test at `test_smTickLayers.js` pins only `reservationFor(0, 1) === 0` ("disabled stays disabled") — the parallel case `reservationFor(0, 3)` is unpinned and returns 3.

Suggested fix: honor the explicit disable before the parallel override, e.g.

```js
function reservationFor(mergeSlots, validationMutexMax) {
    var slots = mergeSlots || 0;
    if (slots <= 0) return 0;            // explicit disable wins in every mode
    var mutexMax = validationMutexMax || 1;
    return mutexMax > 1 ? mutexMax : slots;
}
```

(and pin `reservationFor(0, 3) === 0` in UT-10's helper test).

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: any same-tick merge overwrites `tickMergeSlotSpent` and can overdraw the workflow cap**

`attemptMergeProbe` is shared by four callers (merge_pr, the validate-armed latch-skip, the post-conclude probe, the gh-1101 fast path), and every successful merge lands here:

```js
tickMergeSlotSpent = 'merged';
```

That unconditionally overwrites a `'dispatched'` set earlier in the same tick. Concrete scenario (gh-837 parallel mode makes it reachable — `validate-armed`'s limit rises to the mutex cap):

1. cap 3, serial reservation 1 → upfront hold: `remaining = 2`.
2. `validate-armed` dispatches CI for approved candidate **A** → `spent = 'dispatched'` (validate_pr dispatches don't decrement `remaining`, the held unit *is* A's slot).
3. Later in the same L3 pass the same rule processes approved candidate **B** — `ai_validated` latched + green + CLEAN → the latch-skip probe **merges B** → `spent = 'merged'`.
4. L3→L4 boundary: `spent === 'merged'` → the whole reservation is refunded (`remaining = min(initial, 2 + 1) = 3`).
5. Agent legs dispatch 3 reviews. Real workflow dispatches this tick: **4** (A + 3 reviews) against cap 3.

A's validation is still in flight, so the width is not actually free — the refund double-counts it and the tick oversubscribes the cap by ~1 dispatch (in parallel mode, by up to `mutexMax − 1`). It self-corrects next tick via `ensureWorkflowBudgetActiveCount`, but the cap is a hard runner-cost ceiling, not a hint.

Suggested fix: first resolution wins — don't overwrite an existing spend:

```js
if (!tickMergeSlotSpent) tickMergeSlotSpent = 'merged';
```

(conservative: after a dispatch + an unrelated merge, the width stays held, which is the safe direction), or track the merge per-PR and refund only when no merge-path validation spent the width this tick.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: move verification uses a post-push re-read — ticket E4 prescribes the push's own sha**

```js
newHeadMtt = freshHeadSha(effectiveRepoInfo, ticket.prNumber);
```

The `movedThisTick` record — the guard the whole freshness-before-verdicts fix rests on — is only as fresh as this read. The ticket's edge case E4 (input/gh-1114/ticket.md, "Edge cases") says explicitly:

> E4 — `headMoved` read stale by API lag (seen 2026-10-19 16:43) → use the sha returned by the update/push itself, not a re-read.

This implementation is a re-read (`github_get_pr`), not the push's own sha. If that read hits the same read-after-write lag that was already observed live on 2026-10-19, it returns the *old* sha → `headMoved` is false → the move is **not recorded** → L2 verdicts run on the superseded head and can re-park/re-merge exactly the #435 false verdict this card exists to kill — silently, with no log line (the failure is indistinguishable from "nothing moved"). The failure mode is fail-open toward the bug being fixed.

It never behaves *worse* than today (E1/E3 handling is correct, and the L1→L2 cache drop still helps), which is why this is not blocking — but please confirm the mechanism against E4: `silentUpdateBranch` runs the push in a git checkout, so the pushed sha is available locally (`git rev-parse HEAD` right after the push, or the push output) and would make the record lag-immune at zero extra API cost. If the re-read is a deliberate trade-off, a one-line comment superseding E4 would prevent the next reviewer from re-raising it.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

💡 **SUGGESTION: an unresolved pre-push head (`uHead === null`) records a move that never happened**

```js
if (headMoved(uHead, newHeadMtt)) {
```

In the "no resolvable head sha" branch (the heal backstop) `uHead` is `null` while `refreshHeadSilent` still runs. `headMoved(null, sha)` returns `true` for *any* sha — including an up-to-date no-op refresh (park-reset's non-BEHIND path merges cleanly with no push). Result: the PR lands in `tickMovedPrs` spuriously, its L2 verdicts *and* its merge-candidate validation are deferred for a tick even though the head never changed.

The impact is conservative (a lost tick, never a wrong verdict) and the window is narrow (head resolve failed *and* the post-push read succeeded *and* nothing moved), so this is polish — but E1's own contract in the comment above says "an unverified move records nothing". One token makes it hold:

```js
if (uHead && headMoved(uHead, newHeadMtt)) {
```

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the L1→L2 cache drop only drops the global repo's cache**

```js
dropOpenPrsCache(globalRepoInfo);
```

Rules can carry `configPath` / per-rule repositories (`effectiveRepoInfo` ≠ `globalRepoInfo`); the ioCache is keyed per (owner, repo), so a multi-repo custom `smRules` tick keeps a stale cached open-PR list for every non-global repo across the L1→L2 boundary — exactly the staleness this boundary exists to remove. The deployed `sm_github.json` is single-repo, so nothing is broken today; this is a latent gap for project customizations.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **Additions**: +1601
- **Deletions**: -66
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T19:27:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T23:45:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1114
### What changed
Layered the SM tick (gh-1114): `sm_github.json` rules now run in layers — L0 hygiene → **L1 freshness** (unarm-stale / silent-update / park-reset) → L2 verdict (merge / fail / arm / sweep) → L3 dispatch → L4 agents → L5 close — so a head that this tick's freshness rules moved can never be judged by verdicts that read the superseded head (live #435 false park). Added a merge-first capacity reservation so agent lanes can no longer outrun the approved merge path under the workflow cap.

### Key decisions
- New pure leaf module `js/common/smRuleLayers.js`: rule-id → layer map, verdict-action set, merge-path predicate, `mergeReservedSlots`/`reservationFor` math (hoisted require, gh-823 rule)
- `movedThisTick` guard (AC7/AC12): only verified moves record (fresh post-push `github_get_pr` read — E1/E4); DRY ticks never record or claim deferrals (E3); fresh (non-approved) validations keep today's same-tick flow
- L1→L2 boundary drops the `openPrs` ioCache so verdict queries re-read current heads
- Merge-first capacity (AC9-13): reservation held upfront from the dispatch budget; released unused at the L3 boundary (I7) or fully after a merge; in gh-837 parallel mode it equals `validationMutexMax`; `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots: 0` restores today's behavior bit-for-bit (jira-mode ticks never reserve)
- Rule order moved exactly one rule class (unarm-stale-validation into L1, ahead of merge-validated — disjoint query sets, no merge lost); #682/#637/red-yields-slot/gh-994 relative orders preserved and pinned by tests

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smTickLayers.json   # UT-1/AC6 layer-map suite (new)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # full suite: 4764 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  R["sm_github.json rules"] --> L["smRuleLayers.js layer map"]
  L --> T["SM tick (action)"]
  T --> L1["L1 freshness: unarm / silent-update / park-reset"]
  L1 -->|"head moved → tickMovedPrs + openPrs cache drop"| L2["L2 verdict: merge / fail / arm / sweep"]
  L2 -->|"movedThisTick → defer (AC7)"| L3["L3 dispatch: validate-armed before fresh (AC13)"]
  L3 -->|"reservation released / spent"| L4["L4 agent legs (capacity-aware)"]
  L4 --> L5["L5 close"]
```
</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1120._

> ℹ️ **6 resolved thread(s) excluded; 11 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the `mergeReservedSlots: 0` kill switch is inert in gh-837 parallel mode**

`mergeReservedSlots` documents `0` / `false` / `'false'` as *disabling* the reservation — "bit-identical with the pre-gh-1114 capacity behavior" (this module's own docstring at line 156, the PR description, and the ticket's rollback story all rely on it). But `reservationFor` ignores the disabled value whenever parallel validation is active:

```js
function reservationFor(mergeSlots, validationMutexMax) {
    var slots = mergeSlots || 0;
    var mutexMax = validationMutexMax || 1;
    return mutexMax > 1 ? mutexMax : slots;   // slots=0 is overridden when mutexMax>1
}
```

So a project that sets `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots: 0` (or `false`) as an emergency kill switch **still reserves the whole parallel width** on every gh-837 tick: agent lanes are throttled to `initial − validationMutexMax` until the L3 boundary, and when a merge-path validation dispatches, one unit of the cap is held for the whole tick. That is not "today's behavior bit-for-bit".

Note the test at `test_smTickLayers.js` pins only `reservationFor(0, 1) === 0` ("disabled stays disabled") — the parallel case `reservationFor(0, 3)` is unpinned and returns 3.

Suggested fix: honor the explicit disable before the parallel override, e.g.

```js
function reservationFor(mergeSlots, validationMutexMax) {
    var slots = mergeSlots || 0;
    if (slots <= 0) return 0;            // explicit disable wins in every mode
    var mutexMax = validationMutexMax || 1;
    return mutexMax > 1 ? mutexMax : slots;
}
```

(and pin `reservationFor(0, 3) === 0` in UT-10's helper test).

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: any same-tick merge overwrites `tickMergeSlotSpent` and can overdraw the workflow cap**

`attemptMergeProbe` is shared by four callers (merge_pr, the validate-armed latch-skip, the post-conclude probe, the gh-1101 fast path), and every successful merge lands here:

```js
tickMergeSlotSpent = 'merged';
```

That unconditionally overwrites a `'dispatched'` set earlier in the same tick. Concrete scenario (gh-837 parallel mode makes it reachable — `validate-armed`'s limit rises to the mutex cap):

1. cap 3, serial reservation 1 → upfront hold: `remaining = 2`.
2. `validate-armed` dispatches CI for approved candidate **A** → `spent = 'dispatched'` (validate_pr dispatches don't decrement `remaining`, the held unit *is* A's slot).
3. Later in the same L3 pass the same rule processes approved candidate **B** — `ai_validated` latched + green + CLEAN → the latch-skip probe **merges B** → `spent = 'merged'`.
4. L3→L4 boundary: `spent === 'merged'` → the whole reservation is refunded (`remaining = min(initial, 2 + 1) = 3`).
5. Agent legs dispatch 3 reviews. Real workflow dispatches this tick: **4** (A + 3 reviews) against cap 3.

A's validation is still in flight, so the width is not actually free — the refund double-counts it and the tick oversubscribes the cap by ~1 dispatch (in parallel mode, by up to `mutexMax − 1`). It self-corrects next tick via `ensureWorkflowBudgetActiveCount`, but the cap is a hard runner-cost ceiling, not a hint.

Suggested fix: first resolution wins — don't overwrite an existing spend:

```js
if (!tickMergeSlotSpent) tickMergeSlotSpent = 'merged';
```

(conservative: after a dispatch + an unrelated merge, the width stays held, which is the safe direction), or track the merge per-PR and refund only when no merge-path validation spent the width this tick.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: move verification uses a post-push re-read — ticket E4 prescribes the push's own sha**

```js
newHeadMtt = freshHeadSha(effectiveRepoInfo, ticket.prNumber);
```

The `movedThisTick` record — the guard the whole freshness-before-verdicts fix rests on — is only as fresh as this read. The ticket's edge case E4 (input/gh-1114/ticket.md, "Edge cases") says explicitly:

> E4 — `headMoved` read stale by API lag (seen 2026-10-19 16:43) → use the sha returned by the update/push itself, not a re-read.

This implementation is a re-read (`github_get_pr`), not the push's own sha. If that read hits the same read-after-write lag that was already observed live on 2026-10-19, it returns the *old* sha → `headMoved` is false → the move is **not recorded** → L2 verdicts run on the superseded head and can re-park/re-merge exactly the #435 false verdict this card exists to kill — silently, with no log line (the failure is indistinguishable from "nothing moved"). The failure mode is fail-open toward the bug being fixed.

It never behaves *worse* than today (E1/E3 handling is correct, and the L1→L2 cache drop still helps), which is why this is not blocking — but please confirm the mechanism against E4: `silentUpdateBranch` runs the push in a git checkout, so the pushed sha is available locally (`git rev-parse HEAD` right after the push, or the push output) and would make the record lag-immune at zero extra API cost. If the re-read is a deliberate trade-off, a one-line comment superseding E4 would prevent the next reviewer from re-raising it.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

💡 **SUGGESTION: an unresolved pre-push head (`uHead === null`) records a move that never happened**

```js
if (headMoved(uHead, newHeadMtt)) {
```

In the "no resolvable head sha" branch (the heal backstop) `uHead` is `null` while `refreshHeadSilent` still runs. `headMoved(null, sha)` returns `true` for *any* sha — including an up-to-date no-op refresh (park-reset's non-BEHIND path merges cleanly with no push). Result: the PR lands in `tickMovedPrs` spuriously, its L2 verdicts *and* its merge-candidate validation are deferred for a tick even though the head never changed.

The impact is conservative (a lost tick, never a wrong verdict) and the window is narrow (head resolve failed *and* the post-push read succeeded *and* nothing moved), so this is polish — but E1's own contract in the comment above says "an unverified move records nothing". One token makes it hold:

```js
if (uHead && headMoved(uHead, newHeadMtt)) {
```

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the L1→L2 cache drop only drops the global repo's cache**

```js
dropOpenPrsCache(globalRepoInfo);
```

Rules can carry `configPath` / per-rule repositories (`effectiveRepoInfo` ≠ `globalRepoInfo`); the ioCache is keyed per (owner, repo), so a multi-repo custom `smRules` tick keeps a stale cached open-PR list for every non-global repo across the L1→L2 boundary — exactly the staleness this boundary exists to remove. The deployed `sm_github.json` is single-repo, so nothing is broken today; this is a latent gap for project customizations.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1120
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1120
- **Title**: gh-1114 SM: layered tick order + merge-first capacity — freshness before verdicts, merge path reserved (minimal, no semantic changes)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1114` → `main`
- **State**: closed
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +1601
- **Deletions**: -66
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T19:27:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T23:45:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1114
### What changed
Layered the SM tick (gh-1114): `sm_github.json` rules now run in layers — L0 hygiene → **L1 freshness** (unarm-stale / silent-update / park-reset) → L2 verdict (merge / fail / arm / sweep) → L3 dispatch → L4 agents → L5 close — so a head that this tick's freshness rules moved can never be judged by verdicts that read the superseded head (live #435 false park). Added a merge-first capacity reservation so agent lanes can no longer outrun the approved merge path under the workflow cap.

### Key decisions
- New pure leaf module `js/common/smRuleLayers.js`: rule-id → layer map, verdict-action set, merge-path predicate, `mergeReservedSlots`/`reservationFor` math (hoisted require, gh-823 rule)
- `movedThisTick` guard (AC7/AC12): only verified moves record (fresh post-push `github_get_pr` read — E1/E4); DRY ticks never record or claim deferrals (E3); fresh (non-approved) validations keep today's same-tick flow
- L1→L2 boundary drops the `openPrs` ioCache so verdict queries re-read current heads
- Merge-first capacity (AC9-13): reservation held upfront from the dispatch budget; released unused at the L3 boundary (I7) or fully after a merge; in gh-837 parallel mode it equals `validationMutexMax`; `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots: 0` restores today's behavior bit-for-bit (jira-mode ticks never reserve)
- Rule order moved exactly one rule class (unarm-stale-validation into L1, ahead of merge-validated — disjoint query sets, no merge lost); #682/#637/red-yields-slot/gh-994 relative orders preserved and pinned by tests

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smTickLayers.json   # UT-1/AC6 layer-map suite (new)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # full suite: 4764 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  R["sm_github.json rules"] --> L["smRuleLayers.js layer map"]
  L --> T["SM tick (action)"]
  T --> L1["L1 freshness: unarm / silent-update / park-reset"]
  L1 -->|"head moved → tickMovedPrs + openPrs cache drop"| L2["L2 verdict: merge / fail / arm / sweep"]
  L2 -->|"movedThisTick → defer (AC7)"| L3["L3 dispatch: validate-armed before fresh (AC13)"]
  L3 -->|"reservation released / spent"| L4["L4 agent legs (capacity-aware)"]
  L4 --> L5["L5 close"]
```
</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1120._

> ℹ️ **6 resolved thread(s) excluded; 11 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the `mergeReservedSlots: 0` kill switch is inert in gh-837 parallel mode**

`mergeReservedSlots` documents `0` / `false` / `'false'` as *disabling* the reservation — "bit-identical with the pre-gh-1114 capacity behavior" (this module's own docstring at line 156, the PR description, and the ticket's rollback story all rely on it). But `reservationFor` ignores the disabled value whenever parallel validation is active:

```js
function reservationFor(mergeSlots, validationMutexMax) {
    var slots = mergeSlots || 0;
    var mutexMax = validationMutexMax || 1;
    return mutexMax > 1 ? mutexMax : slots;   // slots=0 is overridden when mutexMax>1
}
```

So a project that sets `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots: 0` (or `false`) as an emergency kill switch **still reserves the whole parallel width** on every gh-837 tick: agent lanes are throttled to `initial − validationMutexMax` until the L3 boundary, and when a merge-path validation dispatches, one unit of the cap is held for the whole tick. That is not "today's behavior bit-for-bit".

Note the test at `test_smTickLayers.js` pins only `reservationFor(0, 1) === 0` ("disabled stays disabled") — the parallel case `reservationFor(0, 3)` is unpinned and returns 3.

Suggested fix: honor the explicit disable before the parallel override, e.g.

```js
function reservationFor(mergeSlots, validationMutexMax) {
    var slots = mergeSlots || 0;
    if (slots <= 0) return 0;            // explicit disable wins in every mode
    var mutexMax = validationMutexMax || 1;
    return mutexMax > 1 ? mutexMax : slots;
}
```

(and pin `reservationFor(0, 3) === 0` in UT-10's helper test).

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: any same-tick merge overwrites `tickMergeSlotSpent` and can overdraw the workflow cap**

`attemptMergeProbe` is shared by four callers (merge_pr, the validate-armed latch-skip, the post-conclude probe, the gh-1101 fast path), and every successful merge lands here:

```js
tickMergeSlotSpent = 'merged';
```

That unconditionally overwrites a `'dispatched'` set earlier in the same tick. Concrete scenario (gh-837 parallel mode makes it reachable — `validate-armed`'s limit rises to the mutex cap):

1. cap 3, serial reservation 1 → upfront hold: `remaining = 2`.
2. `validate-armed` dispatches CI for approved candidate **A** → `spent = 'dispatched'` (validate_pr dispatches don't decrement `remaining`, the held unit *is* A's slot).
3. Later in the same L3 pass the same rule processes approved candidate **B** — `ai_validated` latched + green + CLEAN → the latch-skip probe **merges B** → `spent = 'merged'`.
4. L3→L4 boundary: `spent === 'merged'` → the whole reservation is refunded (`remaining = min(initial, 2 + 1) = 3`).
5. Agent legs dispatch 3 reviews. Real workflow dispatches this tick: **4** (A + 3 reviews) against cap 3.

A's validation is still in flight, so the width is not actually free — the refund double-counts it and the tick oversubscribes the cap by ~1 dispatch (in parallel mode, by up to `mutexMax − 1`). It self-corrects next tick via `ensureWorkflowBudgetActiveCount`, but the cap is a hard runner-cost ceiling, not a hint.

Suggested fix: first resolution wins — don't overwrite an existing spend:

```js
if (!tickMergeSlotSpent) tickMergeSlotSpent = 'merged';
```

(conservative: after a dispatch + an unrelated merge, the width stays held, which is the safe direction), or track the merge per-PR and refund only when no merge-path validation spent the width this tick.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: move verification uses a post-push re-read — ticket E4 prescribes the push's own sha**

```js
newHeadMtt = freshHeadSha(effectiveRepoInfo, ticket.prNumber);
```

The `movedThisTick` record — the guard the whole freshness-before-verdicts fix rests on — is only as fresh as this read. The ticket's edge case E4 (input/gh-1114/ticket.md, "Edge cases") says explicitly:

> E4 — `headMoved` read stale by API lag (seen 2026-10-19 16:43) → use the sha returned by the update/push itself, not a re-read.

This implementation is a re-read (`github_get_pr`), not the push's own sha. If that read hits the same read-after-write lag that was already observed live on 2026-10-19, it returns the *old* sha → `headMoved` is false → the move is **not recorded** → L2 verdicts run on the superseded head and can re-park/re-merge exactly the #435 false verdict this card exists to kill — silently, with no log line (the failure is indistinguishable from "nothing moved"). The failure mode is fail-open toward the bug being fixed.

It never behaves *worse* than today (E1/E3 handling is correct, and the L1→L2 cache drop still helps), which is why this is not blocking — but please confirm the mechanism against E4: `silentUpdateBranch` runs the push in a git checkout, so the pushed sha is available locally (`git rev-parse HEAD` right after the push, or the push output) and would make the record lag-immune at zero extra API cost. If the re-read is a deliberate trade-off, a one-line comment superseding E4 would prevent the next reviewer from re-raising it.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

💡 **SUGGESTION: an unresolved pre-push head (`uHead === null`) records a move that never happened**

```js
if (headMoved(uHead, newHeadMtt)) {
```

In the "no resolvable head sha" branch (the heal backstop) `uHead` is `null` while `refreshHeadSilent` still runs. `headMoved(null, sha)` returns `true` for *any* sha — including an up-to-date no-op refresh (park-reset's non-BEHIND path merges cleanly with no push). Result: the PR lands in `tickMovedPrs` spuriously, its L2 verdicts *and* its merge-candidate validation are deferred for a tick even though the head never changed.

The impact is conservative (a lost tick, never a wrong verdict) and the window is narrow (head resolve failed *and* the post-push read succeeded *and* nothing moved), so this is polish — but E1's own contract in the comment above says "an unverified move records nothing". One token makes it hold:

```js
if (uHead && headMoved(uHead, newHeadMtt)) {
```

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the L1→L2 cache drop only drops the global repo's cache**

```js
dropOpenPrsCache(globalRepoInfo);
```

Rules can carry `configPath` / per-rule repositories (`effectiveRepoInfo` ≠ `globalRepoInfo`); the ioCache is keyed per (owner, repo), so a multi-repo custom `smRules` tick keeps a stale cached open-PR list for every non-global repo across the L1→L2 boundary — exactly the staleness this boundary exists to remove. The deployed `sm_github.json` is single-repo, so nothing is broken today; this is a latent gap for project customizations.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

So `validationMutexMax = effectiveValidationConcurrency(cfg, approvedQueueDepth)` — it IS queue-gated (only > 1 when the approved queue depth ≥ watermark). The workflow cap comes from `configuredWorkflowCap` (line 8528).

Now the critical question: can `workflowBudget.initial <= tickMergeReservedSlots` (i.e., cap ≤ mutexMax in parallel mode, or cap ≤ mergeReservedSlots=1 in serial mode)?

**Serial mode (default)**: reserved = 1. If cap = 1 (a small project with workflowCap 1): hold 1 → remaining = 0 → NOTHING dispatches all tick — including the merge-path validation (the very thing reserved!). On main today: cap 1 → one dispatch per tick (validate-armed arms the merge candidate in tick 1; it validates; merge in tick 2...). With the PR: remaining = 0 after the upfront hold → `effBudget <= 0` at the rule-level skip → **validate-armed is skipped entirely** → the merge path can NEVER arm → **total merge deadlock** for any layered tick with workflowCap = 1.

Wait — is workflowCap=1 realistic? Let me check where configuredWorkflowCap comes from and its default. Let me grep. In sm_github.json jobParams maybe workflowCap is set. Let me check the default and the deployed value.

Actually, hold on. Let me re-examine: is the merge-path rule really blocked at `remaining <= 0`? In processRule:

```js
var budgetCapped = !rule.localTeammate && !rule.localAction;
var effBudget = (budgetCapped && workflowBudget) ? ruleBudgetRemaining(rule, workflowBudget) : null;
if (effBudget !== null && effBudget <= 0) { skip rule }
``

ruleBudgetRemaining(merge-path rule, held budget) = min(remaining, max(0, initial − reserved)) — per the thread-6 refactor, merge-path and non-merge-path are treated IDENTICALLY now. cap 1, reserved 1: min(max(0,0), max(0, 1−1)) = 0 → skip. YES — the merge-path rule is skipped.

But WAIT — is that actually wrong? Think about what the reservation means with cap 1: the single slot is reserved FOR the merge path. The merge path needs remaining > 0 to dispatch. The hold consumed it. The math gives merge-path rules the same budget as everyone: 0. The reserved slot can never be spent by anyone. Deadlock until... the reservation releases at L3→L4 — but only if the loop gets there! The release fires when `nextLayerIdx > L3_IDX` AFTER a rule with layer ≤ L3... — the release happens in the forEach loop regardless of whether the rule was skipped (processRule returns, then the boundary checks run). So after validate-armed (L3) is skipped, the boundary L3→L4 fires → release → remaining = min(1, 0+1) = 1 → but validate-armed already ran (skipped)! The L4 agent legs then can dispatch with remaining 1 — the reserved slot goes to an AGENT leg, the merge path never validated. Merge path starved — PERMANENTLY (every tick: hold → skip arms → release → agents spend it).

So with workflowCap = 1 and the default mergeReservedSlots = 1, the merge path never arms again. That's a REAL deadlock — the exact opposite of the feature's goal.

And with cap = 2, serial reserved 1: hold → remaining 1. validate-armed (merge-path): ruleBudgetRemaining = min(1, 1) = 1 → dispatch OK (remaining → 0 after spend). Agent legs: min(0,1) = 0 → blocked. Merge-first works. ✓

So the failure is exactly `cap ≤ mergeReservedSlots` (serial default 1) or `cap ≤ mutexMax` (parallel). Is cap=1 plausible for the deployed sm_github.json? Let me check sm_github.json's workflowCap. Also, `configuredWorkflowCap` — where from? Line 8528: `var workflowBudget = configuredWorkflowCap ? {...} : null`. Let me find configuredWorkflowCap's source — probably jobParams.workflowCap or config.workflowCap.

Also — what about mergeReservedSlots default 1 vs cap unset (workflowBudget null)? If workflowBudget is null (no cap configured), the hold is skipped (`if (workflowBudget)`), reservation is computed but no budget to hold — release/hold no-ops. ruleBudgetRemaining returns 0 when !workflowBudget... it's guarded by callers (`workflowBudget &&`). OK.

Goal — SM tick runs in layers: freshness → verdict → dispatch → agents (v1, minimal reorder)
One sentence: **every SM tick first brings PR branches up to date, then judges/merges only heads that did not move this tick, then dispatches validation, then runs agent legs — with zero rule-semantics changes.**

Supersedes #1113 (same problem, narrower fix). Today `sm_github.json` runs verdict rules (6–11) before freshness (12–13). Live epam/dmtools-dart#435 2026-10-19 17:46: `fail-validation` re-parked the PR on stale head `24dbdeca` and posted a false "current head has failing checks" comment; 3 s later `silent-update-behind` in the same tick moved the head to `3f513a8c`. Recovery needed an extra tick.

## Why this framing
- Minimal blood: reorder existing rules + one "moved-this-tick" guard + a post-freshness head re-read. No new rules, no query changes, no action behavior changes.
- Retracted for this card: per-PR single-action state machine (one decision per PR per tick). Valuable but a larger refactor → separate follow-up.

## Architecture
Layers (subject = [REDACTED:Certificate DN], queries and actions; relative order inside each layer = today's order.
```
L0 hygiene      1 rerun-cancelled-checks, 2 rerun-any-cancelled-checks,
                3-5 reconcile-*                       (no head moves)
L1 freshness    6 unarm-stale-validation   (concluded + BEHIND → frees ai_validating)
                12 silent-update-behind    (notLabels ai_validating — unchanged)
                13 park-reset
L2 verdict      7 merge-validated, 8 fail-validation,
                9 rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, 10 rework-on-validation-failed,
                11 sweep-stale-validating
L3 dispatch     14-18 validate-*, 19 validated-green
L4 agents       20 conflict-rework … 34 review-on-issue-label
L5 close        35 close-on-merge
```
Mechanism:
- `movedThisTick: Set<prNumber>` in the tick; filled by `update_branch` (and park-reset's update) whenever the head actually moved (`headMoved` — after/before sha differ).
- L2 actions (`merge_pr`, `fail_validation`, `arm_rework`, `sweep_stale_validation`) skip PRs in `movedThisTick` with a log line `⏭ pr-N head moved this tick — verdict deferred`.
- After L1, the openPrs ioCache is dropped (pattern already used by fail-validation) so L2 queries read current heads.

Invariants:
- **I1** — no rule query, label set or action semantics change; diff = order in `sm_github.json` + guard + cache drop.
- **I2** — a head under running validation is never moved (keeps `notLabels: ai_validating` on silent-update-behind).
- **I3** — existing order constraints hold: #682 reconcile first; #637 merge-validated before sweep-stale-validating; "red yields the slot" fail-validation before validate-armed; gh-994 park-reset on any head change.
- **I4** — no merge of a head that moved this tick (it has no checks yet; strict protection would refuse anyway).
- **I5** — moved PR is never parked/reworked/commented in the same tick.

Risk check of the one real move (unarm-stale-validation into L1, ahead of merge-validated): its query is concluded + BEHIND; merge-validated needs mergeState CLEAN — disjoint sets, so no merge is lost.


## Merge-first capacity (owner directive 2026-10-19)
Subject = **the merge pipeline** (the oldest approved PR, FIFO). Each tick, capacity goes first to whatever brings an approved PR closer to merge; agent legs get only what is left.

Priority of capacity within one tick:
1. **Merge** an approved head that is green and CLEAN (`merge-validated`). Costs no workflow budget.
2. **Freshen the merge candidate**: update the oldest approved PR if it is BEHIND. Fires no CI, so it costs no budget.
3. **Validate the merge candidate** (`validate-armed` / `revalidate-*`). This takes a **reserved** slot from the workflow cap and the validation mutex.
4. Everything else: `validate-fresh`, `conflict-rework`, rework, dev, review. These use the remaining budget.

Mechanism (still minimal):
- The workflow budget gets `reservedForMerge = 1` (configurable, `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots`). L4 rules and `validate-fresh` can spend only `cap - reservedForMerge` until L3 has decided for the merge candidate. If L3 did not use the slot (no candidate, already running, or moved this tick), the slot is released to L4 in the same tick.
- With parallel validation (gh-837, queue ≥ watermark), the reservation equals `validationMutexMax`. Approved PRs always win the mutex over fresh, non-approved validations.
- Rework on an approved PR whose validation went red (`rework-on-red-*`) is a merge-path leg: it goes before review/dev legs of non-approved PRs when the budget is short.

Invariants:
- **I6**: an approved, mergeable-after-validation PR is never starved by review/dev/rework dispatches of other PRs in the same tick.
- **I7**: the reservation never blocks agent legs when there is no merge candidate (no idle cap).
- **I8**: the FIFO rule is unchanged: only the oldest approved PR is the candidate (or the top N under gh-837 parallel mode).

Acceptance criteria:
- **AC9**: tick with cap = 3, one approved PR needing validation and 4 PRs needing review: validation of the approved PR is dispatched and at most 2 reviews (UT-6).
- **AC10**: same tick without an approved candidate: 3 reviews dispatched (UT-7).
- **AC11**: the approved candidate is green + CLEAN: merged first, and the reservation is released to agent legs (UT-8).
- **AC12**: the approved candidate is BEHIND: updated, not validated in this tick (moved), and its slot is released (UT-9).
- **AC13**: gh-837 parallel mode (queue ≥ watermark): reservation = mutexMax, and fresh validations never take a slot ahead of approved ones (UT-10).
- **AC14**: decision-diff replay (AC8) is extended with a "busy tick" fixture: merge throughput is no worse than the current order (IT-4).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — #435 replay (BEHIND, red on old head): tick updates branch, no validation_failed label, no park comment; next tick dispatches CI (IT-1).
- **AC2** — up-to-date red → parked exactly as today (REG-1).
- **AC3** — green + CLEAN + approved → merged in the same tick as today (REG-2).
- **AC4** — ai_validating running → branch not updated (REG-3).
- **AC5** — concluded green but BEHIND → unarmed, updated, revalidated next tick, merged after (IT-2).
- **AC6** — layer order asserted by a unit test over `sm_github.json` (rule ids → layer map); adding a rule without a layer fails the test (UT-1).
- **AC7** — guard: L2 actions are no-ops for `movedThisTick` PRs (UT-2..5, one per action).
- **AC8** — decision-diff replay: recorded tick inputs for fa + dart (≥5 PR states incl. #435, #1591 guest-park, green-merge, conflict, review-stale) produce identical actions on old vs new order except the BEHIND cases listed in AC1/AC5 (IT-3).

## Test plan
- `UT-*` in `js/unit-tests`: order map, guard per action, cache drop.
- `IT-*` SM tick harness with stubbed GitHub reads: AC1, AC5, AC8 replays.
- `REG-*`: existing rule-order tests (#682, #637, red-yields-slot, gh-994) unchanged and green. A red REG blocks merge even when UT/IT are green.
- Rollout: release, watch 3 live ticks on dart + fa; rollback = revert the single commit (order-only).

### Edge cases
- **E1** — update push fails (fork without workflows perm, #1106) → head not moved, not in set, L2 behaves as today.
- **E2** — main moves between L1 and L2 → PR becomes BEHIND again; L2 merge refuses (not CLEAN), next tick L1 updates.
- **E3** — dry-run → no real move; dry logs must not claim deferral.
- **E4** — `headMoved` read stale by API lag (seen 2026-10-19 16:43) → use the sha returned by the update/push itself, not a re-read.

## Non-goals
- New rules, rule query changes, label semantics (capacity reservation is budget accounting only, not a new rule).
- Per-PR single-action state machine (follow-up).
- Fork push permissions (#1106), stamp quoting (#1107), sweep-check-runs 502 tolerance.

- epam/dmtools-dart#435 (tick run 39296737688), #436; IstiN/dmtools-agents#1113 (superseded), #1106, #1107; gh-994, #682, #637.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8.
