## PR Description

Closes #1114
### What changed
Layered the SM tick (gh-1114): `sm_github.json` rules now run in layers — L0 hygiene → **L1 freshness** (unarm-stale / silent-update / park-reset) → L2 verdict (merge / fail / arm / sweep) → L3 dispatch → L4 agents → L5 close — so a head that this tick's freshness rules moved can never be judged by verdicts that read the superseded head (live #435 false park). Added a merge-first capacity reservation so agent lanes can no longer outrun the approved merge path under the workflow cap.

### Key decisions
- New pure leaf module `js/common/smRuleLayers.js`: rule-id → layer map, verdict-action set, merge-path predicate, `mergeReservedSlots`/`reservationFor` math (hoisted require, gh-823 rule)
- `movedThisTick` guard (AC7/AC12): only verified moves record (fresh post-push `github_get_pr` read — E1/E4); DRY ticks never record or claim deferrals (E3); fresh (non-approved) validations keep today's same-tick flow
- L1→L2 boundary drops the `openPrs` ioCache so verdict queries re-read current heads
- Merge-first capacity (AC9-13): reservation held upfront from the dispatch budget; released unused at the L3 boundary (I7) or fully after a merge; in gh-837 parallel mode it equals `validationMutexMax`; `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots: 0` restores today's behavior bit-for-bit (jira-mode ticks never reserve)
- Rule order moved exactly one rule class (unarm-stale-validation into L1, ahead of merge-validated — disjoint query sets, no merge lost); #682/#637/red-yields-slot/gh-994 relative orders preserved and pinned by tests

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smTickLayers.json   # UT-1/AC6 layer-map suite (new)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # full suite: 4764 passed, 0 failed
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD

  L --> T["SM tick (action)"]
  T --> L1["L1 freshness: unarm / silent-update / park-reset"]

  L2 -->|"movedThisTick → defer (AC7)"| L3["L3 dispatch: validate-armed before fresh (AC13)"]
  L3 -->|"reservation released / spent"| L4["L4 agent legs (capacity-aware)"]

```

+/**
+ * gh-1114 — SM tick layering: the rule-id → layer map for the deployed
+ * sm_github.json tick, plus the merge-first capacity math.
+ *
+ * The SM tick runs in layers (relative order inside each layer = the
+ * sm_github.json order):
+ *
+ *   L0 hygiene    rerun-cancelled-checks, rerun-any-cancelled-checks,
+ *                 reconcile-*                          (no head moves)
+ *   L1 freshness  unarm-stale-validation, silent-update-behind, park-reset
+ *                 (heads may move here — silent branch refreshes)
+ *   L2 verdict    merge-validated, fail-validation, rework-on-red-gate-unlatched,
+ *                 rework-on-validation-failed, sweep-stale-validating
+ *   L3 dispatch   validate-armed/-fresh/-masked-green, revalidate-armed(-green),
+ *                 validated-green
+ *   L4 agents     conflict-rework … review-on-issue-label
+ *   L5 close      close-on-merge
+ *
+ * Freshness before verdicts: a head this tick's L1 rules moved carries no
+ * checks yet, so an L2 verdict read against the superseded head is a false
+ * verdict (live epam/dmtools-dart#435: fail-validation re-parked a PR on a
+ * stale head seconds before silent-update-behind moved it). smAgent guards
+ * the L2 actions with the tick's movedThisTick set and drops the openPrs
+ * ioCache on the L1→L2 boundary so verdict queries read current heads.
+ *
+ * Merge-first capacity (owner directive 2026-10-19): one workflow slot
+ * (jobParams.mergeReservedSlots, or the whole gh-837 parallel width) is
+ * reserved for the approved merge path. L4 dispatch rules and fresh
+ * validations may spend only cap − reserved until L3 has decided for the
+ * merge candidate; an unused reservation is released to agent legs in the
+ * same tick (no idle cap).

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1120._

> ℹ️ **6 resolved thread(s) excluded; 11 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the `mergeReservedSlots: 0` kill switch is inert in gh-837 parallel mode**

`mergeReservedSlots` documents `0` / `false` / `'false'` as *disabling* the reservation — "bit-identical with the pre-gh-1114 capacity behavior" (this module's own docstring at line 156, the PR description, and the ticket's rollback story all rely on it). But `reservationFor` ignores the disabled value whenever parallel validation is active:

```js
function reservationFor(mergeSlots, validationMutexMax) {
    var slots = mergeSlots || 0;
    var mutexMax = validationMutexMax || 1;
    return mutexMax > 1 ? mutexMax : slots;   // slots=0 is overridden when mutexMax>1
}
```

So a project that sets `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots: 0` (or `false`) as an emergency kill switch **still reserves the whole parallel width** on every gh-837 tick: agent lanes are throttled to `initial − validationMutexMax` until the L3 boundary, and when a merge-path validation dispatches, one unit of the cap is held for the whole tick. That is not "today's behavior bit-for-bit".

Note the test at `test_smTickLayers.js` pins only `reservationFor(0, 1) === 0` ("disabled stays disabled") — the parallel case `reservationFor(0, 3)` is unpinned and returns 3.

Suggested fix: honor the explicit disable before the parallel override, e.g.

```js
function reservationFor(mergeSlots, validationMutexMax) {
    var slots = mergeSlots || 0;
    if (slots <= 0) return 0;            // explicit disable wins in every mode
    var mutexMax = validationMutexMax || 1;
    return mutexMax > 1 ? mutexMax : slots;
}
```

(and pin `reservationFor(0, 3) === 0` in UT-10's helper test).

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: any same-tick merge overwrites `tickMergeSlotSpent` and can overdraw the workflow cap**

`attemptMergeProbe` is shared by four callers (merge_pr, the validate-armed latch-skip, the post-conclude probe, the gh-1101 fast path), and every successful merge lands here:

```js
tickMergeSlotSpent = 'merged';
```

That unconditionally overwrites a `'dispatched'` set earlier in the same tick. Concrete scenario (gh-837 parallel mode makes it reachable — `validate-armed`'s limit rises to the mutex cap):

1. cap 3, serial reservation 1 → upfront hold: `remaining = 2`.
2. `validate-armed` dispatches CI for approved candidate **A** → `spent = 'dispatched'` (validate_pr dispatches don't decrement `remaining`, the held unit *is* A's slot).
3. Later in the same L3 pass the same rule processes approved candidate **B** — `ai_validated` latched + green + CLEAN → the latch-skip probe **merges B** → `spent = 'merged'`.
4. L3→L4 boundary: `spent === 'merged'` → the whole reservation is refunded (`remaining = min(initial, 2 + 1) = 3`).
5. Agent legs dispatch 3 reviews. Real workflow dispatches this tick: **4** (A + 3 reviews) against cap 3.

A's validation is still in flight, so the width is not actually free — the refund double-counts it and the tick oversubscribes the cap by ~1 dispatch (in parallel mode, by up to `mutexMax − 1`). It self-corrects next tick via `ensureWorkflowBudgetActiveCount`, but the cap is a hard runner-cost ceiling, not a hint.

Suggested fix: first resolution wins — don't overwrite an existing spend:

```js
if (!tickMergeSlotSpent) tickMergeSlotSpent = 'merged';
```

(conservative: after a dispatch + an unrelated merge, the width stays held, which is the safe direction), or track the merge per-PR and refund only when no merge-path validation spent the width this tick.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: move verification uses a post-push re-read — ticket E4 prescribes the push's own sha**

```js
newHeadMtt = freshHeadSha(effectiveRepoInfo, ticket.prNumber);
```

The `movedThisTick` record — the guard the whole freshness-before-verdicts fix rests on — is only as fresh as this read. The ticket's edge case E4 (input/gh-1114/ticket.md, "Edge cases") says explicitly:

> E4 — `headMoved` read stale by API lag (seen 2026-10-19 16:43) → use the sha returned by the update/push itself, not a re-read.

This implementation is a re-read (`github_get_pr`), not the push's own sha. If that read hits the same read-after-write lag that was already observed live on 2026-10-19, it returns the *old* sha → `headMoved` is false → the move is **not recorded** → L2 verdicts run on the superseded head and can re-park/re-merge exactly the #435 false verdict this card exists to kill — silently, with no log line (the failure is indistinguishable from "nothing moved"). The failure mode is fail-open toward the bug being fixed.

It never behaves *worse* than today (E1/E3 handling is correct, and the L1→L2 cache drop still helps), which is why this is not blocking — but please confirm the mechanism against E4: `silentUpdateBranch` runs the push in a git checkout, so the pushed sha is available locally (`git rev-parse HEAD` right after the push, or the push output) and would make the record lag-immune at zero extra API cost. If the re-read is a deliberate trade-off, a one-line comment superseding E4 would prevent the next reviewer from re-raising it.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

💡 **SUGGESTION: an unresolved pre-push head (`uHead === null`) records a move that never happened**

```js
if (headMoved(uHead, newHeadMtt)) {
```

In the "no resolvable head sha" branch (the heal backstop) `uHead` is `null` while `refreshHeadSilent` still runs. `headMoved(null, sha)` returns `true` for *any* sha — including an up-to-date no-op refresh (park-reset's non-BEHIND path merges cleanly with no push). Result: the PR lands in `tickMovedPrs` spuriously, its L2 verdicts *and* its merge-candidate validation are deferred for a tick even though the head never changed.

The impact is conservative (a lost tick, never a wrong verdict) and the window is narrow (head resolve failed *and* the post-push read succeeded *and* nothing moved), so this is polish — but E1's own contract in the comment above says "an unverified move records nothing". One token makes it hold:

```js
if (uHead && headMoved(uHead, newHeadMtt)) {
```

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the L1→L2 cache drop only drops the global repo's cache**

```js
dropOpenPrsCache(globalRepoInfo);
```

Rules can carry `configPath` / per-rule repositories (`effectiveRepoInfo` ≠ `globalRepoInfo`); the ioCache is keyed per (owner, repo), so a multi-repo custom `smRules` tick keeps a stale cached open-PR list for every non-global repo across the L1→L2 boundary — exactly the staleness this boundary exists to remove. The deployed `sm_github.json` is single-repo, so nothing is broken today; this is a latent gap for project customizations.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

Now the critical question: can `workflowBudget.initial <= tickMergeReservedSlots` (i.e., cap ≤ mutexMax in parallel mode, or cap ≤ mergeReservedSlots=1 in serial mode)?

**Serial mode (default)**: reserved = 1. If cap = 1 (a small project with workflowCap 1): hold 1 → remaining = 0 → NOTHING dispatches all tick — including the merge-path validation (the very thing reserved!). On main today: cap 1 → one dispatch per tick (validate-armed arms the merge candidate in tick 1; it validates; merge in tick 2...). With the PR: remaining = 0 after the upfront hold → `effBudget <= 0` at the rule-level skip → **validate-armed is skipped entirely** → the merge path can NEVER arm → **total merge deadlock** for any layered tick with workflowCap = 1.

Wait — is workflowCap=1 realistic? Let me check where configuredWorkflowCap comes from and its default. Let me grep. In sm_github.json jobParams maybe workflowCap is set. Let me check the default and the deployed value.

Actually, hold on. Let me re-examine: is the merge-path rule really blocked at `remaining <= 0`? In processRule:

```js
var budgetCapped = !rule.localTeammate && !rule.localAction;
var effBudget = (budgetCapped && workflowBudget) ? ruleBudgetRemaining(rule, workflowBudget) : null;
if (effBudget !== null && effBudget <= 0) { skip rule }
``

ruleBudgetRemaining(merge-path rule, held budget) = min(remaining, max(0, initial − reserved)) — per the thread-6 refactor, merge-path and non-merge-path are treated IDENTICALLY now. cap 1, reserved 1: min(max(0,0), max(0, 1−1)) = 0 → skip. YES — the merge-path rule is skipped.

But WAIT — is that actually wrong? Think about what the reservation means with cap 1: the single slot is reserved FOR the merge path. The merge path needs remaining > 0 to dispatch. The hold consumed it. The math gives merge-path rules the same budget as everyone: 0. The reserved slot can never be spent by anyone. Deadlock until... the reservation releases at L3→L4 — but only if the loop gets there! The release fires when `nextLayerIdx > L3_IDX` AFTER a rule with layer ≤ L3... — the release happens in the forEach loop regardless of whether the rule was skipped (processRule returns, then the boundary checks run). So after validate-armed (L3) is skipped, the boundary L3→L4 fires → release → remaining = min(1, 0+1) = 1 → but validate-armed already ran (skipped)! The L4 agent legs then can dispatch with remaining 1 — the reserved slot goes to an AGENT leg, the merge path never validated. Merge path starved — PERMANENTLY (every tick: hold → skip arms → release → agents spend it).

So with workflowCap = 1 and the default mergeReservedSlots = 1, the merge path never arms again. That's a REAL deadlock — the exact opposite of the feature's goal.

And with cap = 2, serial reserved 1: hold → remaining 1. validate-armed (merge-path): ruleBudgetRemaining = min(1, 1) = 1 → dispatch OK (remaining → 0 after spend). Agent legs: min(0,1) = 0 → blocked. Merge-first works. ✓

Let me find configuredWorkflowCap's source — probably jobParams.workflowCap or config.workflowCap.

Also — what about mergeReservedSlots default 1 vs cap unset (workflowBudget null)? If workflowBudget is null (no cap configured), the hold is skipped (`if (workflowBudget)`), reservation is computed but no budget to hold — release/hold no-ops. ruleBudgetRemaining returns 0 when !workflowBudget... it's guarded by callers (`workflowBudget &&`). Goal — SM tick runs in layers: freshness → verdict → dispatch → agents (v1, minimal reorder)
One sentence: **every SM tick first brings PR branches up to date, then judges/merges only heads that did not move this tick, then dispatches validation, then runs agent legs — with zero rule-semantics changes.**

Supersedes #1113 (same problem, narrower fix). Today `sm_github.json` runs verdict rules (6–11) before freshness (12–13). Live epam/dmtools-dart#435 2026-10-19 17:46: `fail-validation` re-parked the PR on stale head `24dbdeca` and posted a false "current head has failing checks" comment; 3 s later `silent-update-behind` in the same tick moved the head to `3f513a8c`. Recovery needed an extra tick.

## Why this framing
- Minimal blood: reorder existing rules + one "moved-this-tick" guard + a post-freshness head re-read. No new rules, no query changes, no action behavior changes.
- Retracted for this card: per-PR single-action state machine (one decision per PR per tick). Valuable but a larger refactor → separate follow-up.

## Architecture
Layers (subject = [REDACTED:Certificate DN], queries and actions; relative order inside each layer = today's order.
```
L0 hygiene      1 rerun-cancelled-checks, 2 rerun-any-cancelled-checks,
                3-5 reconcile-*                       (no head moves)
L1 freshness    6 unarm-stale-validation   (concluded + BEHIND → frees ai_validating)
                12 silent-update-behind    (notLabels ai_validating — unchanged)
                13 park-reset
L2 verdict      7 merge-validated, 8 fail-validation,
                9 rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, 10 rework-on-validation-failed,
                11 sweep-stale-validating
L3 dispatch     14-18 validate-*, 19 validated-green
L4 agents       20 conflict-rework … 34 review-on-issue-label
L5 close        35 close-on-merge
```
Mechanism:
- `movedThisTick: Set<prNumber>` in the tick; filled by `update_branch` (and park-reset's update) whenever the head actually moved (`headMoved` — after/before sha differ).
- L2 actions (`merge_pr`, `fail_validation`, `arm_rework`, `sweep_stale_validation`) skip PRs in `movedThisTick` with a log line `⏭ pr-N head moved this tick — verdict deferred`.
- After L1, the openPrs ioCache is dropped (pattern already used by fail-validation) so L2 queries read current heads.

Invariants:
- **I1** — no rule query, label set or action semantics change; diff = order in `sm_github.json` + guard + cache drop.
- **I2** — a head under running validation is never moved (keeps `notLabels: ai_validating` on silent-update-behind).
- **I3** — existing order constraints hold: #682 reconcile first; #637 merge-validated before sweep-stale-validating; "red yields the slot" fail-validation before validate-armed; gh-994 park-reset on any head change.
- **I4** — no merge of a head that moved this tick (it has no checks yet; strict protection would refuse anyway).
- **I5** — moved PR is never parked/reworked/commented in the same tick.

Risk check of the one real move (unarm-stale-validation into L1, ahead of merge-validated): its query is concluded + BEHIND; merge-validated needs mergeState CLEAN — disjoint sets, so no merge is lost.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1120
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1120
- **Title**: gh-1114 SM: layered tick order + merge-first capacity — freshness before verdicts, merge path reserved (minimal, no semantic changes)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1114` → `main`
- **State**: closed
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +1601
- **Deletions**: -66
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T19:27:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T23:45:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1114
### What changed
Layered the SM tick (gh-1114): `sm_github.json` rules now run in layers — L0 hygiene → **L1 freshness** (unarm-stale / silent-update / park-reset) → L2 verdict (merge / fail / arm / sweep) → L3 dispatch → L4 agents → L5 close — so a head that this tick's freshness rules moved can never be judged by verdicts that read the superseded head (live #435 false park). Added a merge-first capacity reservation so agent lanes can no longer outrun the approved merge path under the workflow cap.

### Key decisions
- New pure leaf module `js/common/smRuleLayers.js`: rule-id → layer map, verdict-action set, merge-path predicate, `mergeReservedSlots`/`reservationFor` math (hoisted require, gh-823 rule)
- `movedThisTick` guard (AC7/AC12): only verified moves record (fresh post-push `github_get_pr` read — E1/E4); DRY ticks never record or claim deferrals (E3); fresh (non-approved) validations keep today's same-tick flow
- L1→L2 boundary drops the `openPrs` ioCache so verdict queries re-read current heads
- Merge-first capacity (AC9-13): reservation held upfront from the dispatch budget; released unused at the L3 boundary (I7) or fully after a merge; in gh-837 parallel mode it equals `validationMutexMax`; `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots: 0` restores today's behavior bit-for-bit (jira-mode ticks never reserve)
- Rule order moved exactly one rule class (unarm-stale-validation into L1, ahead of merge-validated — disjoint query sets, no merge lost); #682/#637/red-yields-slot/gh-994 relative orders preserved and pinned by tests

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smTickLayers.json   # UT-1/AC6 layer-map suite (new)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # full suite: 4764 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  R["sm_github.json rules"] --> L["smRuleLayers.js layer map"]
  L --> T["SM tick (action)"]
  T --> L1["L1 freshness: unarm / silent-update / park-reset"]
  L1 -->|"head moved → tickMovedPrs + openPrs cache drop"| L2["L2 verdict: merge / fail / arm / sweep"]
  L2 -->|"movedThisTick → defer (AC7)"| L3["L3 dispatch: validate-armed before fresh (AC13)"]
  L3 -->|"reservation released / spent"| L4["L4 agent legs (capacity-aware)"]
  L4 --> L5["L5 close"]
```
</details>

+ *   L1 freshness  unarm-stale-validation, silent-update-behind, park-reset

+ *   L2 verdict    merge-validated, fail-validation, rework-on-red-gate-unlatched,
+ *                 rework-on-validation-failed, sweep-stale-validating
+ *   L3 dispatch   validate-armed/-fresh/-masked-green, revalidate-armed(-green),
+ *                 validated-green
+ *   L4 agents     conflict-rework … review-on-issue-label
+ *   L5 close      close-on-merge

+ * Freshness before verdicts: a head this tick's L1 rules moved carries no
+ * checks yet, so an L2 verdict read against the superseded head is a false

+ *
+ * Merge-first capacity (owner directive 2026-10-19): one workflow slot
+ * (jobParams.mergeReservedSlots, or the whole gh-837 parallel width) is
+ * reserved for the approved merge path. L4 dispatch rules and fresh
+ * validations may spend only cap − reserved until L3 has decided for the
+ * merge candidate; an unused reservation is released to agent legs in the
+ * same tick (no idle cap).

+    'validate-fresh': 'L3',

`mergeReservedSlots` documents `0` / `false` / `'false'` as *disabling* the reservation — "bit-identical with the pre-gh-1114 capacity behavior" (this module's own docstring at line 156, the PR description, and the ticket's rollback story all rely on it). But `reservationFor` ignores the disabled value whenever parallel validation is active:

```js
function reservationFor(mergeSlots, validationMutexMax) {
    var slots = mergeSlots || 0;
    var mutexMax = validationMutexMax || 1;
    return mutexMax > 1 ? mutexMax : slots;   // slots=0 is overridden when mutexMax>1
}
```

So a project that sets `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots: 0` (or `false`) as an emergency kill switch **still reserves the whole parallel width** on every gh-837 tick: agent lanes are throttled to `initial − validationMutexMax` until the L3 boundary, and when a merge-path validation dispatches, one unit of the cap is held for the whole tick. That is not "today's behavior bit-for-bit".

Note the test at `test_smTickLayers.js` pins only `reservationFor(0, 1) === 0` ("disabled stays disabled") — the parallel case `reservationFor(0, 3)` is unpinned and returns 3.

Suggested fix: honor the explicit disable before the parallel override, e.g.

```js
function reservationFor(mergeSlots, validationMutexMax) {
    var slots = mergeSlots || 0;
    if (slots <= 0) return 0;            // explicit disable wins in every mode
    var mutexMax = validationMutexMax || 1;
    return mutexMax > 1 ? mutexMax : slots;
}
```

(and pin `reservationFor(0, 3) === 0` in UT-10's helper test).

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: any same-tick merge overwrites `tickMergeSlotSpent` and can overdraw the workflow cap**

`attemptMergeProbe` is shared by four callers (merge_pr, the validate-armed latch-skip, the post-conclude probe, the gh-1101 fast path), and every successful merge lands here:

```js
tickMergeSlotSpent = 'merged';
```

That unconditionally overwrites a `'dispatched'` set earlier in the same tick. Concrete scenario (gh-837 parallel mode makes it reachable — `validate-armed`'s limit rises to the mutex cap):

1. cap 3, serial reservation 1 → upfront hold: `remaining = 2`.
2. `validate-armed` dispatches CI for approved candidate **A** → `spent = 'dispatched'` (validate_pr dispatches don't decrement `remaining`, the held unit *is* A's slot).
3. Later in the same L3 pass the same rule processes approved candidate **B** — `ai_validated` latched + green + CLEAN → the latch-skip probe **merges B** → `spent = 'merged'`.
4. L3→L4 boundary: `spent === 'merged'` → the whole reservation is refunded (`remaining = min(initial, 2 + 1) = 3`).
5. Agent legs dispatch 3 reviews. Real workflow dispatches this tick: **4** (A + 3 reviews) against cap 3.

A's validation is still in flight, so the width is not actually free — the refund double-counts it and the tick oversubscribes the cap by ~1 dispatch (in parallel mode, by up to `mutexMax − 1`). It self-corrects next tick via `ensureWorkflowBudgetActiveCount`, but the cap is a hard runner-cost ceiling, not a hint.

Suggested fix: first resolution wins — don't overwrite an existing spend:

```js
if (!tickMergeSlotSpent) tickMergeSlotSpent = 'merged';
```

(conservative: after a dispatch + an unrelated merge, the width stays held, which is the safe direction), or track the merge per-PR and refund only when no merge-path validation spent the width this tick.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: move verification uses a post-push re-read — ticket E4 prescribes the push's own sha**

```js
newHeadMtt = freshHeadSha(effectiveRepoInfo, ticket.prNumber);
```

The `movedThisTick` record — the guard the whole freshness-before-verdicts fix rests on — is only as fresh as this read. The ticket's edge case E4 (input/gh-1114/ticket.md, "Edge cases") says explicitly:

> E4 — `headMoved` read stale by API lag (seen 2026-10-19 16:43) → use the sha returned by the update/push itself, not a re-read.

This implementation is a re-read (`github_get_pr`), not the push's own sha. If that read hits the same read-after-write lag that was already observed live on 2026-10-19, it returns the *old* sha → `headMoved` is false → the move is **not recorded** → L2 verdicts run on the superseded head and can re-park/re-merge exactly the #435 false verdict this card exists to kill — silently, with no log line (the failure is indistinguishable from "nothing moved"). The failure mode is fail-open toward the bug being fixed.

It never behaves *worse* than today (E1/E3 handling is correct, and the L1→L2 cache drop still helps), which is why this is not blocking — but please confirm the mechanism against E4: `silentUpdateBranch` runs the push in a git checkout, so the pushed sha is available locally (`git rev-parse HEAD` right after the push, or the push output) and would make the record lag-immune at zero extra API cost. If the re-read is a deliberate trade-off, a one-line comment superseding E4 would prevent the next reviewer from re-raising it.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

💡 **SUGGESTION: an unresolved pre-push head (`uHead === null`) records a move that never happened**

```js
if (headMoved(uHead, newHeadMtt)) {
```

In the "no resolvable head sha" branch (the heal backstop) `uHead` is `null` while `refreshHeadSilent` still runs. `headMoved(null, sha)` returns `true` for *any* sha — including an up-to-date no-op refresh (park-reset's non-BEHIND path merges cleanly with no push). Result: the PR lands in `tickMovedPrs` spuriously, its L2 verdicts *and* its merge-candidate validation are deferred for a tick even though the head never changed.

The impact is conservative (a lost tick, never a wrong verdict) and the window is narrow (head resolve failed *and* the post-push read succeeded *and* nothing moved), so this is polish — but E1's own contract in the comment above says "an unverified move records nothing". One token makes it hold:

```js
if (uHead && headMoved(uHead, newHeadMtt)) {
```

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the L1→L2 cache drop only drops the global repo's cache**

```js
dropOpenPrsCache(globalRepoInfo);
```

Rules can carry `configPath` / per-rule repositories (`effectiveRepoInfo` ≠ `globalRepoInfo`); the ioCache is keyed per (owner, repo), so a multi-repo custom `smRules` tick keeps a stale cached open-PR list for every non-global repo across the L1→L2 boundary — exactly the staleness this boundary exists to remove. The deployed `sm_github.json` is single-repo, so nothing is broken today; this is a latent gap for project customizations.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

Goal — SM tick runs in layers: freshness → verdict → dispatch → agents (v1, minimal reorder)
One sentence: **every SM tick first brings PR branches up to date, then judges/merges only heads that did not move this tick, then dispatches validation, then runs agent legs — with zero rule-semantics changes.**

Supersedes #1113 (same problem, narrower fix). Today `sm_github.json` runs verdict rules (6–11) before freshness (12–13). Live epam/dmtools-dart#435 2026-10-19 17:46: `fail-validation` re-parked the PR on stale head `24dbdeca` and posted a false "current head has failing checks" comment; 3 s later `silent-update-behind` in the same tick moved the head to `3f513a8c`. Recovery needed an extra tick.

## Why this framing
- Minimal blood: reorder existing rules + one "moved-this-tick" guard + a post-freshness head re-read. No new rules, no query changes, no action behavior changes.
- Retracted for this card: per-PR single-action state machine (one decision per PR per tick). Valuable but a larger refactor → separate follow-up.

## Architecture
Layers (subject = [REDACTED:Certificate DN], queries and actions; relative order inside each layer = today's order.
```
L0 hygiene      1 rerun-cancelled-checks, 2 rerun-any-cancelled-checks,
                3-5 reconcile-*                       (no head moves)
L1 freshness    6 unarm-stale-validation   (concluded + BEHIND → frees ai_validating)
                12 silent-update-behind    (notLabels ai_validating — unchanged)
                13 park-reset
L2 verdict      7 merge-validated, 8 fail-validation,
                9 rework-on-red-gate-unlatched, 10 rework-on-validation-failed,
                11 sweep-stale-validating
L3 dispatch     14-18 validate-*, 19 validated-green
L4 agents       20 conflict-rework … 34 review-on-issue-label
L5 close        35 close-on-merge
```
Mechanism:
- `movedThisTick: Set<prNumber>` in the tick; filled by `update_branch` (and park-reset's update) whenever the head actually moved (`headMoved` — after/before sha differ).
- L2 actions (`merge_pr`, `fail_validation`, `arm_rework`, `sweep_stale_validation`) skip PRs in `movedThisTick` with a log line `⏭ pr-N head moved this tick — verdict deferred`.
- After L1, the openPrs ioCache is dropped (pattern already used by fail-validation) so L2 queries read current heads.

Invariants:
- **I1** — no rule query, label set or action semantics change; diff = order in `sm_github.json` + guard + cache drop.
- **I2** — a head under running validation is never moved (keeps `notLabels: ai_validating` on silent-update-behind).
- **I3** — existing order constraints hold: #682 reconcile first; #637 merge-validated before sweep-stale-validating; "red yields the slot" fail-validation before validate-armed; gh-994 park-reset on any head change.
- **I4** — no merge of a head that moved this tick (it has no checks yet; strict protection would refuse anyway).
- **I5** — moved PR is never parked/reworked/commented in the same tick.

Risk check of the one real move (unarm-stale-validation into L1, ahead of merge-validated): its query is concluded + BEHIND; merge-validated needs mergeState CLEAN — disjoint sets, so no merge is lost.

That would be "the reserved slot IS the validation's slot": hold 1 reserves it; validation dispatch should NOT decrement further (the hold was its slot); agents spend the remaining 2. The implementation: validation DOES decrement (remaining 2 → 1 via the standard dispatch accounting at line 5163), so agents get 1, not 2. And in parallel mode: hold = mutexMax = N. Arms dispatch up to N (limit raised to N): each decrements remaining. remaining after hold = cap − N. The arms run first and consume the budget; fresh gets what's left. Since arms' limit = N and remaining = cap − N... if cap − N < N, arms take all of it, fresh gets 0. ✓ "fresh never takes a slot ahead of approved" holds by order.)

Serial mode, cap 1, reserved 1 (default): remaining 0 after hold → validate-armed SKIPPED (effBudget 0) → merge path never validates. With the hold clamped to min(reserved, remaining − ... no...

Actually here's the cleaner view: the hold should reserve slots by making them unspendable by NON-merge-path rules, while merge-path rules see remaining + reserved (or just: not capped by the hold). The current implementation instead subtracts the reservation from the shared pool and lets merge-path draw from the shrunken pool. For cap > reserved this approximates the intent. For cap ≤ reserved it zeroes the pool and starves everyone including the merge path.

The fix shape: hold `remaining = max(remaining − reserved, 0)` BUT let merge-path rules see the untouched pool: `ruleBudgetRemaining(mergePath) = workflowBudget.remaining + held` — which is exactly what the deleted merge-path exemption did (return raw remaining before the hold was subtracted... no wait, the hold already mutated remaining).

So even an un-reserved leftover slot goes to the arm first (order), and the min() cap throttles agents. I.e. hold = min(reserved, remaining − 1?) — but if remaining=1, hold 0: but then a non-merge-path L3 rule (validate-fresh comes AFTER validate-armed in order)... validate-fresh is L3, AFTER validate-armed. Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1120._

> ℹ️ **6 resolved thread(s) excluded; 11 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the `mergeReservedSlots: 0` kill switch is inert in gh-837 parallel mode**

`mergeReservedSlots` documents `0` / `false` / `'false'` as *disabling* the reservation — "bit-identical with the pre-gh-1114 capacity behavior" (this module's own docstring at line 156, the PR description, and the ticket's rollback story all rely on it). But `reservationFor` ignores the disabled value whenever parallel validation is active:

```js
function reservationFor(mergeSlots, validationMutexMax) {
    var slots = mergeSlots || 0;
    var mutexMax = validationMutexMax || 1;
    return mutexMax > 1 ? mutexMax : slots;   // slots=0 is overridden when mutexMax>1
}
```

So a project that sets `jobParams.mergeReservedSlots: 0` (or `false`) as an emergency kill switch **still reserves the whole parallel width** on every gh-837 tick: agent lanes are throttled to `initial − validationMutexMax` until the L3 boundary, and when a merge-path validation dispatches, one unit of the cap is held for the whole tick. That is not "today's behavior bit-for-bit".

Note the test at `test_smTickLayers.js` pins only `reservationFor(0, 1) === 0` ("disabled stays disabled") — the parallel case `reservationFor(0, 3)` is unpinned and returns 3.

Suggested fix: honor the explicit disable before the parallel override, e.g.

```js
function reservationFor(mergeSlots, validationMutexMax) {
    var slots = mergeSlots || 0;
    if (slots <= 0) return 0;            // explicit disable wins in every mode
    var mutexMax = validationMutexMax || 1;
    return mutexMax > 1 ? mutexMax : slots;
}
```

(and pin `reservationFor(0, 3) === 0` in UT-10's helper test).

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: any same-tick merge overwrites `tickMergeSlotSpent` and can overdraw the workflow cap**

`attemptMergeProbe` is shared by four callers (merge_pr, the validate-armed latch-skip, the post-conclude probe, the gh-1101 fast path), and every successful merge lands here:

```js
tickMergeSlotSpent = 'merged';
```

That unconditionally overwrites a `'dispatched'` set earlier in the same tick. Concrete scenario (gh-837 parallel mode makes it reachable — `validate-armed`'s limit rises to the mutex cap):

1. cap 3, serial reservation 1 → upfront hold: `remaining = 2`.
2. `validate-armed` dispatches CI for approved candidate **A** → `spent = 'dispatched'` (validate_pr dispatches don't decrement `remaining`, the held unit *is* A's slot).
3. Later in the same L3 pass the same rule processes approved candidate **B** — `ai_validated` latched + green + CLEAN → the latch-skip probe **merges B** → `spent = 'merged'`.
4. L3→L4 boundary: `spent === 'merged'` → the whole reservation is refunded (`remaining = min(initial, 2 + 1) = 3`).
5. Agent legs dispatch 3 reviews. Real workflow dispatches this tick: **4** (A + 3 reviews) against cap 3.

A's validation is still in flight, so the width is not actually free — the refund double-counts it and the tick oversubscribes the cap by ~1 dispatch (in parallel mode, by up to `mutexMax − 1`). It self-corrects next tick via `ensureWorkflowBudgetActiveCount`, but the cap is a hard runner-cost ceiling, not a hint.

Suggested fix: first resolution wins — don't overwrite an existing spend:

```js
if (!tickMergeSlotSpent) tickMergeSlotSpent = 'merged';
```

(conservative: after a dispatch + an unrelated merge, the width stays held, which is the safe direction), or track the merge per-PR and refund only when no merge-path validation spent the width this tick.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: move verification uses a post-push re-read — ticket E4 prescribes the push's own sha**

```js
newHeadMtt = freshHeadSha(effectiveRepoInfo, ticket.prNumber);
```

The `movedThisTick` record — the guard the whole freshness-before-verdicts fix rests on — is only as fresh as this read. The ticket's edge case E4 (input/gh-1114/ticket.md, "Edge cases") says explicitly:

> E4 — `headMoved` read stale by API lag (seen 2026-10-19 16:43) → use the sha returned by the update/push itself, not a re-read.

This implementation is a re-read (`github_get_pr`), not the push's own sha. If that read hits the same read-after-write lag that was already observed live on 2026-10-19, it returns the *old* sha → `headMoved` is false → the move is **not recorded** → L2 verdicts run on the superseded head and can re-park/re-merge exactly the #435 false verdict this card exists to kill — silently, with no log line (the failure is indistinguishable from "nothing moved"). The failure mode is fail-open toward the bug being fixed.

It never behaves *worse* than today (E1/E3 handling is correct, and the L1→L2 cache drop still helps), which is why this is not blocking — but please confirm the mechanism against E4: `silentUpdateBranch` runs the push in a git checkout, so the pushed sha is available locally (`git rev-parse HEAD` right after the push, or the push output) and would make the record lag-immune at zero extra API cost. If the re-read is a deliberate trade-off, a one-line comment superseding E4 would prevent the next reviewer from re-raising it.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

💡 **SUGGESTION: an unresolved pre-push head (`uHead === null`) records a move that never happened**

```js
if (headMoved(uHead, newHeadMtt)) {
```

In the "no resolvable head sha" branch (the heal backstop) `uHead` is `null` while `refreshHeadSilent` still runs. `headMoved(null, sha)` returns `true` for *any* sha — including an up-to-date no-op refresh (park-reset's non-BEHIND path merges cleanly with no push). Result: the PR lands in `tickMovedPrs` spuriously, its L2 verdicts *and* its merge-candidate validation are deferred for a tick even though the head never changed.

The impact is conservative (a lost tick, never a wrong verdict) and the window is narrow (head resolve failed *and* the post-push read succeeded *and* nothing moved), so this is polish — but E1's own contract in the comment above says "an unverified move records nothing". One token makes it hold:

```js
if (uHead && headMoved(uHead, newHeadMtt)) {
```

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the L1→L2 cache drop only drops the global repo's cache**

```js
dropOpenPrsCache(globalRepoInfo);
```

Rules can carry `configPath` / per-rule repositories (`effectiveRepoInfo` ≠ `globalRepoInfo`); the ioCache is keyed per (owner, repo), so a multi-repo custom `smRules` tick keeps a stale cached open-PR list for every non-global repo across the L1→L2 boundary — exactly the staleness this boundary exists to remove. The deployed `sm_github.json` is single-repo, so nothing is broken today; this is a latent gap for project customizations.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…
